svg.data-what: red bone marrow: the stem cell niche on the bone, the sinusoid, and blood cells in the making

rect.data-what: the marrow space between the bone, filled with blood-forming cells

g.data-what: a sinusoid: a wide, thin-walled vessel that new blood cells squeeze into to reach the circulation

path.data-what: a trabecula of spongy bone; its inner surface, the endosteum, is one of the niches

g.data-what: osteoblasts lining the bone, which also hold blood stem cells near them
stromal cells: reticular cells whose long arms hold the marrow together and feed signals to the blood-forming cells
fat cells, more of them as we age

ellipse.data-what: the endosteal niche: the bone surface, osteoblasts and stromal cells keep blood stem cells quiet and alive

use.data-what: a blood stem cell, resting in its niche; it can make every kind of blood cell

g.data-what: a megakaryocyte, a giant cell with a lobed nucleus; it pushes long arms into the sinusoid that break into platelets
an erythroblastic island: red cell precursors around a nursing macrophage; each will push out its nucleus to become a red cell
white blood cells on their way: blasts, maturing neutrophils, monocytes, lymphocytes
